alternatives: Keep inline styles and add a JS token module (no cascade, no variants, no dark-mode story, and every panel keeps re-implementing a button); CSS modules (solves colocation but not the missing token/variant layer, and shadcn assumes Tailwind); stay on React 18 and fork/pin drei v9 (freezes the viewer on an unmaintained R3F line and blocks postprocessing v3); check tokens.generated.css into git (immediately stale, and reviewers cannot tell whether encoding.ts or the CSS won); enable Tailwind preflight now and accept the restyle (violates the zero-visual-change requirement of the foundation task).
consequences: Chrome can finally be composed and themed instead of hand-styled, and a color can only be changed in encoding.ts. Costs: two styling systems coexist until the last inline-styled panel is migrated, and shadcn components generated before that point may need preflight's resets (border-width, box-sizing) restated locally. Tailwind v4 scans prose for class candidates, so the CSS bundle carries a few kB of inert utilities until real classes replace them. React 19 pins the R3F/drei/postprocessing/three versions together — none can be bumped alone. Under frameloop="demand" any new useFrame animation that forgets invalidate() will silently run for one frame; the audit table is the guard. Two decorative animators (drei <Stars> twinkle, flow particles) still request frames unconditionally, so the loop only truly idles once they sit behind a motion preference.
context: viz/AGENTS.md forbade Tailwind and mandated CSS-in-.css-files-alongside-components, which in practice became inline style objects on every HUD panel: ~2500 lines of unshareable style, no token layer, and colors re-typed as literals next to the scene/encoding.ts tables that are supposed to be the single source of truth. The Astrolabe redesign needs a real component surface (shadcn) across seven tasks, which needs Tailwind; drei v10 / @react-three/postprocessing v3 only ship for React Three Fiber v9, which requires React 19; and the viewer must keep working as a static export opened over file:// with zero network access, so a CDN-hosted font or stylesheet is not an option. Nothing may change visually in the foundation task itself.
decided_by: marcus (design approved in session, recorded by claude)
decision: Tailwind v4 (via @tailwindcss/vite) plus shadcn/ui are permitted in viz/ and supersede the CSS-alongside-components rule; new chrome is written with token-driven utilities, not inline styles. The runtime baseline is React 19 + @react-three/fiber v9 + @react-three/drei v10 + @react-three/postprocessing v3 + three 0.185. Tailwind's preflight is deliberately NOT imported (the CSS entry expands @import "tailwindcss" by hand and omits the base layer) so the surviving inline-styled panels and drei <Html> labels are untouched; the task that removes the last inline-styled surface flips it on. scene/encoding.ts stays the single source of truth for every hue: a build-time bridge (src/styles/tokens.ts, run by the reposkein-tokens Vite plugin at dev and build) renders BRAND / NODE_KIND_META / EDGE_TYPE_META / LANGUAGE_HEX into a deterministic @theme static block at src/styles/tokens.generated.css, which is git-ignored so it cannot become a second source of truth. Fonts are self-hosted woff2 under src/assets/fonts (no external requests, relative URLs under base "./"). The Canvas renders with frameloop="demand": every useFrame animator must invalidate() while active (scene/frameloop.ts holds the audit), and idle camera drift is opt-in. The one-reducer rule holds for state with semantics, but pointer-rate and per-frame values (hover, edge draw counts) move to dedicated useSyncExternalStore channels, and dispatch is a separate context from state — this is not an exception to "no state library", it is how the single reducer stays affordable.
title: Viewer redesign baseline: React 19, Tailwind v4 tokens generated from encoding.ts
